- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) and price drops, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to match true decline.  
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 72–74, forecast often overcorrects downward; if below 68–70, undercorrects upward — apply smoothing to avoid extreme swings.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% to align with observed lagged behavior.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance or apply 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence.
